title: Algebraic prolongations and finite separable extension topologies of a henselian valuation
statement: Let $F$ be a field with a nontrivial valuation $v$ whose valuation ring is henselian [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], and let $E/F$ be a finite algebraic extension [def-pc-field-extension]. A valuation is written additively as $v:F\to\Gamma\cup\{\infty\}$, where $\Gamma=v(F^\times)$ is the value group, a totally ordered abelian group, $v(0)=\infty$, $v(xy)=v(x)+v(y)$ and $v(x+y)\geq\min(v(x),v(y))$. Its topology has the balls $v(x-a)>\gamma$ as a basis, and its valuation ring is $\mathcal O_v=\{x:v(x)\geq0\}$ [def-trf-valuation-ring]. There exists a prolongation of $v$ to $E$, unique up to equivalence of valuations (equality of their valuation subrings); its valuation ring is henselian. The prolonged valuation topology induces the original topology on $F$. If $E/F$ is separable, every valuation topology on $E$ whose induced topology on $F$ is the $v$-topology equals this prolonged topology. Here separable means that every element has a minimal polynomial coprime to its formal derivative [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. No completeness, rank-one, or discrete-value-group hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: XX 4.4, printed p.374, valued-algebraic preliminaries for the forms of Krasner lemma; Bourbaki, Algebre commutative VI section 8 (not locally available). The finite separable topology clause distinguishes equality of topologies from equivalence of valuations.

proof.text: Put $V=\mathcal O_v$ and $C=\{x\in E:x\text{ satisfies a monic polynomial over }V\}$. By [lem-per-valuation-normalization-localizations], $C$ is a nonzero domain integral over $V$, with fraction field $E$. If $e\in C$ is idempotent, $e(e-1)=0$, so $e=0$ or $e=1$. Thus [lem-trf-integral-component-henselian-permanence] applies to $V\to C$ and gives that $C$ is henselian local. This uses integrality, not module-finiteness of $C/V$.

source.place: Tag 092X, lemma-integral-over-henselian; normalization input is the admitted valued-field interface recorded at ILO XX 4.4, p.374.

proof.text: Let $\mathfrak n$ be the unique maximal ideal of $C$. Every denominator outside $\mathfrak n$ is a unit, so $C_{\mathfrak n}=C$ inside $E$. The forward and converse clauses of [lem-per-valuation-normalization-localizations] show that $C$ is a valuation ring, $C\cap F=V$, and every valuation ring of $E$ restricting to $V$ equals $C$. To recover a valuation explicitly, take $\Gamma_C=E^\times/C^\times$, put $[x]\leq[y]$ iff $y/x\in C$, and set $w(x)=[x]$ for $x\ne0$, $w(0)=\infty$. Multiplication by units preserves membership in $C$, so this order is well defined; the valuation-ring alternative makes it total, and membership of both $y/x$ and $x/y$ makes the classes equal. Translation invariance follows by cancelling the translating factor. If $w(x)\leq w(y)$ then $(x+y)/x=1+y/x\in C$, giving the valuation inequality (the zero-sum case is immediate). Its nonnegative ring is $C$. Since $C^\times\cap F^\times=V^\times$, the restriction identifies $F^\times/V^\times$ with an ordered subgroup, and $[a]\mapsto v(a)$ identifies this subgroup with $\Gamma_v$. Thus $w$ prolongs $v$, up to the usual ordered value-group identification. Its ring is henselian by step 1, and the ring uniqueness just proved is exactly uniqueness up to equivalence. The same argument applies to any henselian valuation ring of $F$.

source.place: Tag 00ID, lemma-valuation-group, quotient construction; the two localization clauses are the admitted normalization input for ILO XX 4.4, p.374.

proof.text: For any valuation $t$ on $E$ whose restriction to $F$ is nontrivial, apply [lem-per-algebraic-valuation-coarsening-correspondence]. Write $\Gamma_F=t(F^\times)\subseteq\Gamma_E=t(E^\times)$ and choose $\epsilon>0$ in $\Gamma_F$. For $\delta\geq0$ in $\Gamma_E$, choose $n>0$ with $n\delta\in\Gamma_F$; then $\eta=n\delta+\epsilon\in\Gamma_F$ satisfies $\eta>\delta$. For $\delta<0$, take $\eta=\epsilon$. Hence $\Gamma_F$ is cofinal in $\Gamma_E$. The intersection with $F$ of any zero-ball $t(x)>\delta$ contains the restriction zero-ball $t(x)>\eta$; conversely every restriction zero-ball is the intersection with $F$ of the ball with that same radius in $\Gamma_E$. Translations give equality of the subspace topology and the topology of the restricted valuation. Applying this to $w$ from step 2 proves that its topology induces the original $v$-topology on $F$.

source.place: XX 4.4, printed p.374, valued-field preliminaries; agent-written ball comparison from the admitted torsion value-group input.

proof.text: Now assume $E/F$ separable and let $t$ be any valuation giving a topology on $E$ with the required subspace topology on $F$. Its restriction $u$ to $F$ is nontrivial. Indeed, if $u$ were trivial, the torsion assertion of [lem-per-algebraic-valuation-coarsening-correspondence] would make every element of the ordered group $\Gamma_E$ torsion, hence zero: a positive or negative element cannot have a positive multiple equal to zero. Thus $t$ would be trivial and its topology discrete, whereas the $v$-topology is not discrete: for each radius $\gamma$, a value $\max(\gamma,0)+\epsilon$ with $\epsilon>0$ is attained by a nonzero element in that zero-ball. Step 3 now shows that $u$ and $v$ induce the same topology. Put $T=\mathcal O_t$ and $U=T\cap F$. By [lem-per-valuation-topology-common-coarsening] there is a valuation ring $R\subsetneq F$ containing $V\cup U$. By [lem-per-henselian-valuation-coarsenings], applied to $V\subseteq R$, $R$ is henselian.

source.place: XX 4.4, printed p.374, valued-field preliminaries for the Bourbaki VI section 8 reference; agent-written comparison using the admitted common-coarsening and henselian-coarsening interfaces.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-algebraic-valuation-coarsening-correspondence] to $C\subset E$ over $V\subset F$ and to $T\subset E$ over $U\subset F$. The proper overring $R$ lifts to proper valuation rings $C_R,T_R\subsetneq E$ containing $C,T$, respectively, with $C_R\cap F=T_R\cap F=R$. Apply the already proved steps 1--2 to the henselian valuation ring $R$ and the same finite extension $E/F$: its integral closure is henselian local by [lem-trf-integral-component-henselian-permanence], and [lem-per-valuation-normalization-localizations] identifies every prolonging valuation ring with its localization at the unique maximal ideal. Therefore $C_R=T_R$. This is an application of the previously established prolongation assertion, not of the topology conclusion being proved.

source.place: XX 4.4, printed p.374, valued-field background; agent-written application of the algebraic coarsening correspondence and the henselian normalization argument. Henselian integrality: Stacks Tag 092X, lemma-integral-over-henselian.

proof.text: The common ring $C_R=T_R$ is proper in $E$ and contains both $C$ and $T$. The valuations $w$ and $t$ are nontrivial, since their restrictions to $F$ are nontrivial. Apply [lem-per-valuation-topology-common-coarsening] over $E$ to conclude that their topologies are equal, as required. Separability was not needed in this argument; keeping it in the stated last clause gives precisely the requested assertion, with no completeness or rank assumption.

source.place: XX 4.4, printed p.374, valued-field preliminaries; final common-coarsening comparison.
